readme:
# OpenLoop

**The open control + verification + evolution plane for coding agents.** Plug Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Agent Zero, Hermes, OpenClaw, VoltAgent workflows and other runtimes into one evidence-driven loop without requiring a second model API bill.

No external model API keys are required in the default `host_native` mode. The loop inherits the host’s authentication, model, and tools. Unsupported automation falls back honestly to prompt-file mode.

[![CI](https://github.com/Akshu1245/openloop/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Akshu1245/openloop/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11+-blue.svg)](pyproject.toml)

## Why

Prompt engineering asks you to babysit agents turn-by-turn. **Loop engineering** designs the system that prompts, verifies, budgets, and resumes until a verifiable goal is met.

OpenLoop is the **control plane** — not another paid agent:

- **Host intelligence plane** — your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, …)
- **Deterministic control plane** — phases, checkpoints, HITL, budgets, repair loops
- **Deterministic verification plane** — tests, security, anti-cheat, design audit
- **Governed evolution plane** — verified runs propose improvements; benchmarks decide; promotions are explicit and rollbackable

## Architecture

```text
loop CLI  →  Control Engine (phased, persisted)
                ├─ Host adapters (Claude/Codex/Gemini/OpenCode/JCode/Krater/…)
                ├─ Worktrees + skills + patterns
                ├─ On-demand portable skills + project memory/knowledge graph
                ├─ Evolution queue (propose → scan → benchmark → promote/rollback)
                └─ Verification (git/lint/tests/semgrep/gitleaks/trivy/a11y)
```

## Why this is different

Most agent frameworks optimize the **agent**. OpenLoop governs the space between agents and your repository:

| Problem | OpenLoop answer |
|---|---|
| Every agent has a different CLI/auth/session model | Capability-probed host adapters + honest prompt-file fallback |
| A model says "done" | Git evidence + deterministic verification decides |
| Multi-agent edits collide | Worktree-per-job + dependency graph + explicit merge-back |
| Skills make prompts huge | Metadata-first, on-demand skill selection |
| "Self-improvement" can poison future runs | Verified provenance + quarantine + comparative benchmark gate + rollback |
| Switching runtimes loses project knowledge | Host-neutral context ledger + knowledge graph + portable run packages |

OpenLoop does not train model weights, secretly change its safety policy, or call a candidate "better" because the same agent says so.

## 60-second setup

### Windows PowerShell

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Akshu1245/openloop.git
cd openloop
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -e ".[dev]"
loop init
loop doctor
loop start --goal "Inspect this repository and produce a verified implementation plan" --host prompt_file --no-wait
loop status
loop report
```

### Linux / macOS

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Akshu1245/openloop.git
cd openloop
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]"
loop init
loop doctor
loop start --goal "Inspect this repository and produce a verified implementation plan" --host prompt_file --no-wait
```

Or use `install.ps1` / `install.sh`.

## Host-native default

```yaml
intelligence:
  mode: host_native
  model: inherited
  external_model_calls: false
  provider_fallback: false
```

| Mode | API keys | Fallback providers |
|------|----------|--------------------|
| `host_native` (default) | Not required | Disabled |
| `hybrid` / `external` | Explicit opt-in only | Disabled unless configured |

## Prompt-file workflow

When a host cannot be automated:

1. `loop start --goal "..."` writes `.loop/runs/<id>/NEXT_PROMPT.md`
2. You (or Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Krater) execute that prompt
3. Mark done: write `HOST_DONE.json` or `loop resume <id> --host-done`
4. Loop verifies evidence and either completes, repairs (bounded prompt), or escalates

## Autonomy ladder

| Level | Behaviour | Default |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| L1 | Report-only | — |
| L2 | Assisted worktree writes + HITL | **Yes** |
| L3 | Unattended | Explicit flag + readiness gate |

## Multi-agent orchestration

`loop orchestrate` collects a business brief and creates a durable task graph assigned to editable specialist roles (`.loop/agents/*/AGENT.md`).

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `loop team list` | Specialist roles |
| `loop jobs list` / `loop graph` | Inspect jobs |
| `loop jobs run` | Sequential execution |
| `loop jobs run-parallel --max-parallel N` | Concurrent jobs (worktree-per-job + merge-back) |
| `loop jobs cancel-graph` | Hard-cancel pending **and** running jobs (terminates tracked host processes) |

Each job runs in its own isolated git worktree and merges back with `git merge --no-ff`. A real conflict downgrades the job to failed (no auto-resolve), so dependents never build on unmerged work.

Also included:

- Source-grounded research — `loop research`
- Technical/on-page SEO — `loop seo audit`
- Answer-engine optimization — `loop aeo audit`
- Security scanning with dedup + SBOM — `loop security scan`

See [docs/multi-agent-orchestration.md](docs/multi-agent-orchestration.md).

## Governed self-evolution

Every deterministically verified run can stage reusable context/skill candidates. Staging is automatic; activation is not.

```bash
loop evolve status
loop evolve propose <verified-run-id>
loop evolve show <candidate-id>

# Attach a real baseline-vs-candidate benchmark artifact.
loop evolve evaluate <candidate-id> \
  --baseline-passed 6 --baseline-total 10 \
  --candidate-passed 9 --candidate-total 10 \
  --regressions 0 --evidence reports/evals/candidate.json

loop evolve promote <candidate-id>
loop evolve rollback <candidate-id>
```

Promotion requires at least three baseline and candidate cases, existing evidence, zero regressions, and a strictly higher pass rate. Skill candidates are security-screened before they enter the queue. Prompt/routing candidates may be reviewed but cannot self-activate in v0.2.

See [docs/evolution.md](docs/evolution.md).

## Runtime ecosystem

Agent Zero, Hermes and OpenClaw are optional compatibility adapters. Unknown headless contracts fall back safely instead of guessing commands. VoltAgent is a framework rather than one universal CLI, so its bridge is intentionally explicit:

```bash
export LOOP_VOLTAGENT_CMD='node ./scripts/openloop-runner.mjs --prompt {prompt}'
loop agents
loop start --host voltagent --goal "Fix the failing tests and prove it"
```

No upstream runtime source is vendored by these adapters. See [docs/runtime-ecosystem.md](docs/runtime-ecosystem.md).

## Context engineering

Loop engineering decides *who drives*. Context engineering decides *what the agent is looking at*. Both are deterministic and local.

**Context as a variable** — store the artifact once, hand the host a handle:

```powershell
python -m pytest -q > pytest.log
loop context put pytest_log --file pytest.log
loop context peek pytest_log --grep "^(FAILED|ERROR)" -C 3
```

The prompt receives `@ctx:pytest_log — 4182 lines / 214.6KB` plus a preview, not 214 KB of log. Caps: 4 MB per artifact (explicit truncation marker), 32 KB per peek, coldest-first eviction.

**Durable context files** — what is true about *this* repo, ranked deterministically by confidence, scope and goal overlap:

```powershell
loop context add test-invocation --kind instruction --scope "tests/**" `
  --confidence 0.9 --body "Run ``python -m pytest -q``. Bare pytest misses the src layout."
loop context show --goal "fix the failing auth test"
```

**Self-improvement that can't launder a hallucination** — proposals come only from runs the verification plane passed, are single append-only bullets (≤400 chars, ≤3 per run), are journalled with run id + evidence, auto-apply only at L3, and are revertible:

```powershell
loop context learn                 # propose (read-only)
loop context learn <run-id> --apply
loop context journal
loop context revert
```

No model call in the learning path — proposals are derived from the run record, so the same run always yields the same proposal.

See [docs/context-engineering.md](docs/context-engineering.md).

### Discipline plane — coding principles with a verifier

Karpathy's four LLM-coding principles (think before coding, simplicity first, surgical changes, goal-driven execution) are injected into every bounded-execution prompt as a contract, and each one has a deterministic gate that runs on the resulting diff: size and abstraction budgets, speculative-code shapes, out-of-scope files, orphaned comment deletions, formatting-only churn, and a required declaration block naming every assumption and unresolved ambiguity. Advisory at L1/L2, blocking at L3.

```bash
loop discipline charter                # the contract, as injected
loop discipline check --allow 'src/*'  # score the working tree (CI-ready exit code)
loop discipline journal                # what have my agents been assuming?
```

See [docs/discipline.md](docs/discipline.md).

## Knowledge graph

Every host gets an evidence-tagged map of the project — not just the assistants
somebody wrote a skill file for.

```bash
loop graph build                 # graphify if installed, else a built-in lexical pass
loop graph query "how is the prompt budget enforced?"
loop graph explain "enforce_prompt_budget"
loop graph path "HostTask" "BudgetReport"
loop graph brief --focus "<task>"
```

The graph is compiled into the prompt for **all** 15+ hosts, capped at ~1,400
tokens, and trimmed *first* under budget pressure so orientation can never crowd
out success criteria. Relations carry provenance end to end: `EXTRACTED` (read
from source) versus `INFERRED` (resolved), with inferred edges marked `?` in the
prompt so the host verifies before relying on them. Missing or corrupt graph
degrades the prompt; it never fails a run.

Interoperates with [graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify) and
reads its `graph.json` directly — see
[docs/knowledge-graph.md](docs/knowledge-graph.md).

## Design intelligence

Integrates [VoltAgent/awesome-design-md](https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-design-md) as **pinned, untrusted reference data**:

```powershell
loop design sync
loop design compile --goal "SaaS landing page"
loop design audit
```

Never executes imported Markdown. Compiles an original `DESIGN.md` + `.design-intelligence/`.

## Run export / import

Portable, secret-redacted run packages:

```powershell
loop export <run-id> --output run.zip
loop import-inspect run.zip
loop import run.zip --dry-run
loop import run.zip
```

## Host compatibility

See [docs/compatibility-matrix.md](docs/compatibility-matrix.md). Run `loop agents` for a **live** probe — never trust static claims over capability detection.

| Host | Status |
|------|--------|
| prompt_file | Verified (default test harness) |
| Generic subprocess | Verified (Windows + POSIX process lifecycle) |
| Claude Code / Codex / Gemini | Implemented; native headless depends on local CLI auth |
| OpenCode / JCode / Goose / Aider / OpenHands | Capability-probed; prompt-file fallback when not headless-ready |
| Agent Zero / Hermes / OpenClaw | Compatibility adapter; conservative prompt-file fallback until installed CLI proves headless support |
| VoltAgent | Explicit workflow bridge via `LOOP_VOLTAGENT_CMD` |

## Security model

- Secrets path blocklist + best-effort content redaction
- Dependency / deploy / merge approval gates
- Semgrep / Gitleaks / Trivy when on PATH (honest `available: false` otherwise)
- Anti-cheating on diffs
- Untrusted Markdown sanitization for skills & design catalogue
- Evolution candidates are quarantined on destructive/exfiltration/prompt-override patterns
- Candidate promotion is benchmark-gated and records a drift-safe rollback snapshot
- Safe ZIP import (path traversal, zip bombs, symlink rejection)
- Worktree clean refuses to delete dirty/active trees (unless `--force`, still never active runs)
- SQLite WAL + busy timeout for concurrent job writers

## Testing

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
make check                                   # ruff check . + pytest
pytest -q --cov=uloop --cov-fail-under=70
```

Many tests drive real `git` repositories. In environments that forbid `git`
writes they skip with an explicit reason instead of failing — see
[docs/status.md](docs/status.md) for what is verified and how.

## Honest limitations

- Headless native invoke depends on each host CLI; unconfirmed → prompt-file
- JCode / OpenHands / ACP / MCP are capability-probed scaffolds
- Screenshots / a11y need optional browsers/tools
- Design catalogue references must not be copied as trademarked layouts
- L3 unattended is gated and off by default
- Evolution can stage candidates automatically, but cannot silently promote them
- Prompt/routing evolution never self-activates in v0.2
- Secret redaction is pattern-based, not a guarantee of complete secret removal
